> Pick a branch, tag or commit with autocomplete wherever the web UI asks for one, choose a ref for each app when creating a site, and two fixes: a container user that could break `bench` on some hosts, and stale start-on-boot units that flooded the system journal.

### Upgrade Steps

* [ACTION REQUIRED] Install on 3.6.x or newer: run `sudo cwcli self-update` on a shared install or `cwcli self-update` on a per-user install; it upgrades cwcli and restarts the services that were running.
* [ACTION REQUIRED] If you use start-on-boot, run `cwcli status` after upgrading: it names any boot unit that is out of date and the exact command that rewrites it, for example `cwcli config auto-inspect enable` or `cwcli config cred-bridge enable`.
* [ACTION REQUIRED] Verify: run `cwcli --version` and check that it prints `3.8.0`.

### New Features

* Every web UI field that takes a branch, tag or commit is now an autocomplete: Check out ref, Check out ref discarding local changes, Install apps and Add a community integration suggest refs from the repository the field acts on. Typing a commit hash works without a list row, a failed lookup leaves a normal text field, and the list stays the width of its field so long branch names no longer run off a phone.
* The app pickers (New site and New bench) take a branch, tag or commit for each picked app. A remote app is fetched at that ref. An app the bench already holds is checked out at it first, which moves that app for every site on the bench; the picker, the dialog and the plan all say so before Create site runs.

### Bug Fixes

* `cwcli init`, `start`, `restart` and `scale` no longer give the container's `frappe` user a uid that another account in the Frappe image already holds. This broke `bench` on a root host and on a host whose user is a system account (for example a shared install's service account or a CI runner), where `bench init` failed with exit 127 and left the workspace owned by a system account. cwcli now falls back to the image's own uid 1000 and says so once. A plain `cwcli start` repairs an instance an older cwcli left in that state, and deletes nothing.
* A start-on-boot unit whose `cwcli` was removed, for example after moving from a per-user to the shared install, no longer retries every 10 seconds forever and floods the journal. systemd units now stop after a few failed starts, and the auto-inspect and credential-bridge units find whichever `cwcli` install remains. `cwcli status` and `cwcli doctor` name a stale unit and the command that rewrites or removes it.

### Other Changes

* The Typer dependency is capped below 0.29, because 0.29 changed the parameter API behind `cwcli axi ... --help`; a fresh install resolves a Typer version that works.
